name: Diagnostic Usage & Time-Window Monitor
description: Samples per-process CPU and memory while AegisWin is unlocked, records spikes inside a daily watch window, correlates them with application crash and hang events, tracks which app was in the foreground, and runs the monitors you approve.

subComponents.name: Per-Process CPU & Memory Spikes
subComponents.description: Records processes that cross the CPU or memory threshold during the watch window (sampled every 5 seconds).

subComponents.name: Application Crash & Hang Correlator
subComponents.description: Links Application Error (1000) and Application Hang (1002) events to spikes of the same process in the preceding 10 minutes.

subComponents.name: Foreground App Tracker
subComponents.description: Records which process owned the foreground window each time it changes. Process names only, never window titles.

tools.name: Configure Diagnostic Watch Window
tools.description: Sets the daily time window (24-hour HH:MM; equal start and end means all day), the CPU and memory thresholds, and optionally which process names to watch. Only changes this monitor's own settings, not Windows.

tools.name: Check a Proposed Monitor
tools.description: Validates a monitor rule and returns the plain-language description AegisWin generates from it, its privacy flags, how often it would have fired over the last 30 minutes of the watch window, and any problems. Starts nothing. Use it before activate_monitor.

rule.description: A monitor rule, version 1 (see the usage-monitor README): version, name, schedule {startTime, endTime, days?}, trigger {all|any: 1-8 conditions of type process_cpu, process_memory, system_cpu, system_memory, event, crash, foreground}, cooldownSeconds 60-86400, notify tray|none.

reasoning.description: Why this monitor fits the owner's problem. Shown to the owner as supplied by the requesting agent, cut to 600 characters.

tools.name: Start a Monitor
tools.description: Saves a monitor rule and starts watching for it, or replaces the rule of an existing monitor. Monitors only watch and record; they never run anything or change Windows.

rule.description: A monitor rule, version 1 (see the usage-monitor README): version, name, schedule {startTime, endTime, days?}, trigger {all|any: 1-8 conditions of type process_cpu, process_memory, system_cpu, system_memory, event, crash, foreground}, cooldownSeconds 60-86400, notify tray|none.

replaceId.description: Id of the monitor to replace (for example m3).

tools.name: List Monitors
tools.description: Lists saved monitors with their generated descriptions, whether each is running, paused, or blocked by a turned-off component, and hits since unlock.

tools.name: Pause or Resume a Monitor
tools.description: Pauses a monitor (paused: true) or resumes it (paused: false).

tools.name: Delete a Monitor
tools.description: Deletes a saved monitor. Its hits recorded so far stay until they are purged or AegisWin locks.

tools.name: Describe a Monitor to the AI
tools.description: In the app only: starts a conversation in which the AI asks up to 3 rounds of questions and then proposes a monitor rule. Your text and answers go to the configured LLM. Starts nothing.

request.description: What you want to watch, in your own words.

tools.name: Answer the AI
tools.description: In the app only: answers the AI's questions (an empty answer skips one), says whether it may see running app names, or asks it to propose now.

tools.name: End the Monitor Conversation
tools.description: In the app only: forgets the current monitor conversation.

tools.name: Capture Correlated Diagnostic Clues
tools.description: Returns current system load, top processes by CPU and memory, recorded spikes, crash and hang events from the last 24 hours with related spikes, foreground app changes, and monitor hits.

tools.name: Synthesize Diagnostic Clues with AI
tools.description: Sends a diagnostic snapshot to the LLM service to identify the most likely culprit.

tools.name: Read Monitor History
tools.description: Decrypts the recorded monitor history for the last 1-90 days (default 1): spikes, foreground app changes, monitor hits, and when monitoring started and stopped. Shows the gaps when nothing was monitored and why (sleep, closed, shutdown, crash or power loss, paused), with System log evidence. Returns up to `limit` newest events.

tools.name: Set Monitor History Retention
tools.description: Sets how long the encrypted monitor history is kept: 1-90 days and 8-512 MB, whichever limit is reached first. Shortening it deletes older history files at once.

tools.name: Purge Recorded Telemetry and History
tools.description: Deletes all recorded spikes, foreground app history, and monitor hits, in memory and in the encrypted history files, and replaces the history key so deleted files cannot be read later. Saved monitors are kept.
